findings.title: Global group view permission grants group-management access
findings.body: `canManage()` evaluates both `VIEW` and `MANAGE` scopes for the all-groups resource. This method backs operations such as creating top-level groups, so an administrator granted only the read-only `view` scope can create and modify group hierarchy. `canManage()` must evaluate only the `manage` scope; `view` should remain limited to read/list operations.

findings.title: Member-visible group IDs are derived from authorization-resource IDs
findings.body: `groupResource.getId()` is the ID of the authorization Resource, not the realm GroupModel ID. It is passed back into `hasPermission`, which looks up resources by group-ID name, and it is added to the set later used by user providers as `UserModel.GROUPS`. Consequently, a scoped `view-members`/`manage-members` permission generally cannot match its group and user searches are filtered with IDs that do not identify any group, so members of permitted groups are omitted. Evaluate using the resource name (which is the group ID for this schema) and add that name to `granted`.
